criteria.criterion: jobs::check in crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs returns no violations for a commit on the [history] exempt list (the history walk's tip list; the parent's list for a per-commit check), using the same rule as invariant::check.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff: jobs::check now opens with `if invariant::is_exempt(change, judged, history) { return Ok(Vec::new()); }`. is_exempt uses state.exempt (the tip list) when history is Some and judged.config.history.exempt (the parent's list) otherwise. This is the same logic that used to be inline in invariant::check.

criteria.criterion: The exempt-commit test is shared by invariant::check and jobs::check (one helper), not duplicated.
criteria.evidence: The new `pub fn is_exempt` in invariant.rs replaces the inline block in invariant::check, and jobs::check calls the same function. No copy of the logic remains.

criteria.criterion: A new test in athena-gate builds a history where an exempt commit adds an outcome saying landed and a score.json that would otherwise be flagged; run `cargo test -p athena-gate` to see the history check report no JobRecords violation for it.
criteria.evidence: history::exemption_tests::an_exemption_also_excuses_the_job_records_the_commit_adds passed. It checks that check_history reports no JobRecords violation for the exempt commit. The companion test runs the same records without an exemption and shows both target violations ('this commit is not a valid landing' and 'does not follow'), so the exempt test would fail without the early return. All 50 athena-gate tests passed in the full run.

criteria.criterion: A test shows a non-exempt commit adding the same records is still flagged, and a commit after the exempt one is not excused; run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: the_same_records_in_a_non_exempt_commit_are_flagged passed: it asserts both detail strings for the non-exempt commit. The second half of an_exemption_also_excuses_the_job_records_the_commit_adds adds JOB_B's records after the exempt commit and asserts a JobRecords violation for it; that test passed too.

criteria.criterion: `cargo clippy` is clean, `cargo fmt --check` passes, and `cargo test` passes.
criteria.evidence: All three commands ran in one chain and succeeded. Every test suite reported ok with 0 failures.

criteria.criterion: A decision entry in docs/decisions.md (and a CHANGELOG line) records that an exemption also excuses the records the commit adds, citing D66/D67.
criteria.evidence: docs/decisions.md now has D68, which cites D66 and D67 and corrects D67's line that the jobs' records 'still get the per-record checks' (line 1459). The CHANGELOG 'Added' section has a matching line that cites D68, D66 and D67.

summary: The change passes. I read the diff and ran the commands listed below. Before this change, the `[history] exempt` list was honored only by the governed-content check (`invariant::check`). The job-records check (`jobs::check`) still flagged the records an exempt commit adds, which is why the 9 violations remained. Now the exemption test lives in one shared helper, `invariant::is_exempt`, and both checks call it. In a history walk it reads the tip's exempt list; in a single-commit check it reads the parent's list. Two new tests in `crates/athena-gate/src/history.rs` cover it. In the first, an exempt commit adds a landed outcome and a hand-written score.json, and the history check reports no job-records violation for it. The same test then adds records in a later commit and shows they are still flagged. The second test adds the same records without an exemption and shows both errors from your report: "this commit is not a valid landing" and "does not follow". So the first test would fail without the fix. Decision D68 in `docs/decisions.md` and a CHANGELOG line record the change, cite D66 and D67, and correct D67's statement that these records would still be checked. `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` all passed. Nothing outside the requested scope changed. As the brief scoped out, I did not run the history check against the real repository, so it is not confirmed that the 9 violations on ee4b0dd are now gone.
